#### 2026 pricing changes to be aware of

Google adjusted multi-region pricing in 2026. Nearline multi-region storage increased from $0.010/GB to $0.015/GB per month, while Archive multi-region storage in US and EU regions decreased from $0.004/GB to $0.0024/GB per month. If you set lifecycle policies before 2026, it is worth revisiting them to confirm the tier transitions still make economic sense under the updated rates.

#### Extra storage items that add to the monthly “GB stored”

Besides the object’s raw data, Google counts:

* Custom metadata (each character stored counts as bytes)
* XML multipart uploaded parts until completed or aborted
* Bucket tags: each tag attached to a bucket is billed $0.005 per month

### 2. Costs for data processing in GCP

Google groups “data processing” costs into:

* Operation (request) charges
* Retrieval fees
* Inter-region replication
* Autoclass charges

#### Operation charges (requests)

Operations fall into Free, Class A, and Class B. Pricing depends on what the operation applies to:

* **Listing buckets in a project:** Class A Standard rate always applies
* **Bucket-level operations:** priced by the bucket’s default storage class
* **Tag operations:** priced by the tagged bucket’s default storage class
* **Object operations:** priced by the object’s storage class
* **Changing storage class:** billed as a Class A operation for the destination class

#### Retrieval fees

Retrieval fees apply when you read/copy/move/rewrite object data stored in:

* Nearline: $0.01 per GiB
* Coldline: $0.02 per GiB
* Archive: $0.05 per GiB

Retrieval fees do not apply when the object is in a bucket with Autoclass enabled.

#### Early deletion charges

Early deletion applies when data is deleted or rewritten before the minimum duration ends. Key exceptions:

* Does not apply when Object Lifecycle Management changes the storage class
* Does not apply when the object is in an Autoclass bucket

#### Inter-region replication

Inter-region replication is charged per GiB for data written to dual-region and multi-region buckets. Default replication is $0.02 per GiB in North America and Europe, and higher in some other geos.

#### Autoclass charges

Autoclass adds:

* Management fee: $0.0025 per 1,000 objects stored for 30 days
* Plus a one-time enablement charge under certain conditions

### 3. Cost of networking in Cloud Storage

Google Cloud Storage does not charge for data ingress. Uploading or writing data into a Cloud Storage bucket is always free.

Network charges apply only to data egress — when data is read from a bucket or transferred

out of Google Cloud.

Google Cloud Storage egress falls into three billing categories:

#### Egress within Google Cloud

This includes data sent from Cloud Storage to:

* Other Cloud Storage buckets
* Google Cloud services such as BigQuery or Compute Engine

Pricing depends on the source and destination bucket locations. Reads within the same multi-region are free, which is a meaningful cost advantage for globally distributed apps.

#### General network egress

This applies when data leaves Google Cloud entirely, such as:

* Downloads to the public internet
* Transfers between continents

These charges apply when traffic is not covered by internal Google Cloud routing, specialty services, or Always Free limits.

#### Specialty network services

Specialty egress pricing applies when data uses Google-managed network services, including:

* [Cloud CDN](https://cloud.google.com/cdn/pricing)
* [Cloud Interconnect](https://cloud.google.com/network-connectivity/docs/cdn-interconnect#pricing)
* [CDN Interconnect](https://cloud.google.com/network-connectivity/docs/cdn-interconnect#pricing)
* [Direct Peering](https://cloud.google.com/network-connectivity/docs/direct-peering#pricing)

These services use dedicated network paths, providing higher reliability and performance than general internet egress.

Understanding which egress category your traffic falls into is critical because network transfer is often one of the largest hidden drivers of Google Cloud Storage costs.

### What a real Google Cloud Storage bill looks like

Pricing tables are useful, but a worked example makes the costs tangible. Consider a team storing 1 TB of application data in Standard storage (regional, US) that generates 1 million GET requests and 100 GB of internet egress per month:

* **Storage:** 1,000 GB × $0.020/GB = $20.00
* **GET requests (Class B):** 1,000,000 / 10,000 × $0.004 = $0.40
* **Network egress:** 100 GB × $0.12/GB = $12.00
* **Total:** approximately $32.40/month

Now consider what happens when access patterns shift. If that same 1 TB moves to Archive storage and the team retrieves 50 GB once a year, the monthly picture changes dramatically: $1.20 in storage, $2.50 in retrieval fees during the retrieval month, and minimal egress. Object Lifecycle Management policies can automate that transition based on how recently objects were accessed, which is where most optimization gains come from.

## How To Reduce Your Google Cloud Storage Costs

Beyond using the Google Cloud Console’s built-in billing reports, several strategies can materially lower your GCP storage spend.

**Use Object Lifecycle Management.** Lifecycle rules automatically transition objects between storage classes based on age or access recency. A common pattern: Standard for the first 30 days, Nearline after 30, Coldline after 90, Archive after 365. This prevents stale data from accumulating in expensive tiers — and the transitions themselves are exempt from early deletion charges.

**Right-size your location type.** Multi-region storage delivers higher availability but costs roughly 30% more than regional storage. If your workloads are concentrated in a single geography, regional buckets provide the same durability at a lower price point.

**Keep compute and storage in the same region.** Cross-region egress fees add up quickly. Running your analysis workloads (BigQuery, Compute Engine, GKE) in the same region as your storage buckets eliminates most network transfer costs entirely.

**Consolidate small files.** Google Cloud Storage charges a 128 KB minimum billable size for Nearline, Coldline, and Archive tiers. Storing millions of small log files in cold tiers inflates the bill disproportionately. Batching small files into compressed archives before transitioning them reduces both storage and request costs.

For a broader look at controlling cloud spend across all GCP services, see our guide to [GCP cost optimization](https://www.cloudzero.com/blog/gcp-cost-optimization-tools/).

## How To View, Understand, And Optimize Your Google Cloud Storage Costs The Easier Way

Understanding Google Cloud Storage costs doesn’t require complex analysis. [CloudZero](https://www.cloudzero.com/) provides fast, interactive, and accurate cost visibility using the dimensions you care about. CloudZero uses a code-driven approach to collect, analyze, and share your cloud costs, using the dimensions you care about.

Rather than simply showing your overall or average storage consumption for a month, CloudZero shows you specifics, such as the people, products, or processes driving your storage bill.

That includes the [cost per individual customer](https://www.cloudzero.com/solutions/cost-per-customer), per project, per product, per team, per engineering environment, and more. Per hour, per container, per deployment — you get the picture.

![CloudZero](https://www.cloudzero.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/01/ingest-allocate-analyze-engage.webp)

This includes organizations with incomplete cost allocation tags or multi-tenant environments. You’ll still see how much you spend per customer so that you can charge them profitably on an individual basis.

## GCP Storage Pricing FAQs

### What factors affect Google Cloud Storage pricing?

Google Cloud Storage pricing depends on storage class, location, GB stored per month, data retrieval, request operations, early deletion fees, and network egress charges.

### What are the four Google Cloud Storage classes?

The four Google Cloud Storage classes are Standard, Nearline, Coldline, and Archive. Each class is priced based on access frequency and minimum storage duration.

### How much does Google Cloud Storage cost per GB?

Pricing starts at (regional, US, as of 2026):

* Standard: from $0.020 per GB/month
* Nearline: from $0.010 per GB/month
* Coldline: from $0.004 per GB/month
* Archive: from $0.0012 per GB/month

Prices vary by location type and region. Multi-region storage is more expensive than regional storage.

### Does Google Cloud Storage charge for data ingress?

No. Google Cloud does not charge for data ingress into Cloud Storage buckets. You only pay for storage, access, and data egress.

### Are there retrieval fees in Google Cloud Storage?

Yes. Retrieval fees apply to Nearline ($0.01/GB), Coldline ($0.02/GB), and Archive ($0.05/GB) storage. Standard storage has no retrieval charges.

### What are early deletion charges in Google Cloud Storage?

Early deletion charges apply when data is removed or rewritten before the minimum storage duration ends, except when Autoclass or lifecycle policies handle the transition.

### Does Google Cloud Storage charge for API requests?

Yes. Google Cloud charges for storage operations based on request type: Free, Class A, or Class B. Pricing depends on the object’s storage class and location.

### How does region vs dual-region vs multi-region pricing differ?

Regional storage stores data in one location. Dual-region stores data in two regions within a continent. Multi-region stores data across multiple regions and incurs higher costs due to greater availability and redundancy.

### Is Google Cloud Storage cheaper than Amazon S3?

It depends. For standard hot storage, Google Cloud Storage ($0.020/GB regional) slightly undercuts AWS S3 ($0.023/GB). However, total costs vary based on storage class, retrieval frequency, egress volume, and location. Workload patterns matter more than headline prices.

### Can I automatically move data between GCP storage classes?

Yes. Google Cloud supports Object Lifecycle Management and Autoclass, which automatically move objects between storage tiers based on access patterns.

### How can I see what’s driving my Google Cloud Storage costs?

Native GCP billing shows usage totals, but tools like CloudZero show storage costs by customer, product, team, environment, and workload for deeper cost analysis.

This is a comprehensive guide to Google Cloud Storage pricing published on CloudZero's blog (May 1, 2026). It explains how GCP storage costs are structured and how to optimize them.

**Core Pricing Components:**
- **Storage classes:** Four tiers — Standard (hot data, $0.020/GB/month regional), Nearline (monthly access, $0.010/GB), Coldline (quarterly, $0.004/GB), Archive (yearly, $0.0012/GB). Prices vary by region and location type (Regional, Dual-region, Multi-region).
- **Location types:** Regional (single area, lowest cost), Dual-region (two regions), Multi-region (highest availability, ~30% more expensive).
- **Key cost drivers:** Storage class, data volume, data processing fees (API requests), retrieval fees (Nearline $0.01/GB, Coldline $0.02/GB, Archive $0.05/GB), early deletion charges (30/90/365-day minimums), networking egress charges, and inter-region replication.

**2026 Pricing Changes:** Nearline multi-region increased from $0.010/GB to $0.015/GB per month; Archive multi-region in US/EU decreased from $0.004/GB to $0.0024/GB per month.

**Billing Details:** No charge for data ingress. Storage is billed by object's storage class (not bucket's default), prorated sub-second. Extra storage items billed include custom metadata, XML multipart uploads, and bucket tags ($0.005/month each). Autoclass adds a management fee of $0.0025 per 1,000 objects stored for 30 days.

**Cost Optimization Strategies:**
1. Use Object Lifecycle Management to auto-transition between storage classes
2. Right-size location type (regional vs multi-region)
3. Keep compute and storage in the same region to avoid cross-region egress fees
4. Consolidate small files before storing in cold tiers (128 KB minimum billable size for Nearline, Coldline, Archive)

**Example Bill:** 1 TB Standard storage (regional, US) with 1M GET requests and 100 GB internet egress = ~$32.40/month.

**Comparison:** GCP Standard ($0.020/GB regional) slightly undercuts AWS S3 ($0.023/GB), but total costs depend on workload patterns.

## How Much Does Cloud Storage Cost?

Cloud storage cost refers to the expenses associated with using cloud-based services to store data. It varies depending on factors like data volume, frequency of access, and chosen storage solutions. Understanding these costs is important to plan and budget for cloud investments. Evaluating providers and pricing models can help in optimizing costs while ensuring organizations receive the storage features, reliability and performance they need.

Cloud storage costs typically include fees based on storage volume and duration, as well as additional charges that may arise from data retrieval, transfer, and management. These costs can be influenced by geographical data distribution, compliance requirements, and the need for redundancy. In addition, many providers offer several storage tiers that provide lower cost in exchange for slower performance or limited retrieval.

Another important aspect impacting storage costs is the type of cloud storage service:

* **Block storage** is suitable for databases or applications requiring frequent read/write operations. It offers high performance and is often priced higher due to its speed and reliability.
* **File storage**, resembling traditional storage systems, supports hierarchical file organization and is suitable for document storing and sharing. It usually provides a balance between cost and performance.
* **Object storage** is optimized for handling large volumes of unstructured data, such as media files. It is usually the most scalable and cost-effective option for massive data volumes.

This is part of a series of articles about [cloud costs](https://n2ws.com/blog/cloud-costs)

**In this article:**

* [Key Factors Influencing Cloud Storage Pricing](#keys)
* [Cloud Storage Pricing Models](#pricing)
* [Comparing Major Cloud Storage Provider Pricing](#compare)
* [7 Cost Optimization Strategies for Cloud Storage](#strategy)

## Key Factors Influencing Cloud Storage Pricing

Here are the main factors that influence the cost of cloud storage:

### 1. Storage Capacity and Data Size

Providers typically charge based on the amount of data stored, often priced per gigabyte or terabyte. Larger data sizes translate directly into higher costs. Adjusting storage usage efficiently can lead to considerable [cloud cost savings](/blog/cloud-cost-savings) without sacrificing data access needs. Regular audits can ensure that storage is optimized and unused data is cleared.

Data growth over time can inflate storage costs significantly. As organizations generate more data, they must continually assess their storage needs and adjust plans accordingly. Using data compression and deduplication strategies can help in managing storage size and associated costs.

### 2. Data Durability and Availability Requirements

Cloud providers offer various levels of data durability, represented in terms like nines (e.g., “six nines” or 99.9999%), reflecting the likelihood of lost data. Higher durability guarantees often come with increased costs. Organizations must balance data safety with cost efficiency, selecting durability levels that align with their critical data needs.

Availability requirements, indicating how accessible data is, are another consideration influencing costs. High availability ensures minimal downtime but often increases expenses due to the need for additional resources.

**TIP**: Consider how multi-cloud redundancy can reduce costs while maintaining high durability.

### 3. Data Access Frequency and Retrieval Patterns

Frequently accessed data, or “hot” data, typically incurs higher costs due to the resources required for quick retrieval. “Cold” data, accessed less frequently, benefits from lower costs. Providers often designate tiers for these different access patterns, making tiered storage an effective cost management solution.

Retrieval patterns, including the size and frequency of data retrieval, also add to the cost structure. High retrieval rates can lead to increased bandwidth and processing, inflating costs. By categorizing data based on access necessity and adjusting storage policies accordingly, organizations can optimize their expenditure on cloud storage.

### 4. Data Transfer and Egress Costs

Data transfer and egress costs are often overlooked but crucial elements of cloud storage pricing. They refer to fees charged for moving data in and out of the cloud provider’s network. Higher transfer volumes can lead to substantial additional costs. Understanding these charges and their implications can help organizations plan data movement and prevent budget overruns.

Strategically managing data transfers through practices like local data retrieval, compression, or using multi-region caching can help reduce these costs. Additionally, organizations can take advantage of data transfer credits or free-tier offerings provided by some cloud vendors.

### 5. Geographic Location of Data Storage

Data housed in regions with more expensive infrastructure or stricter regulatory requirements may incur higher costs. Additionally, cross-region data transfers add further expense, prompting organizations to evaluate their geographic needs carefully. Choosing data centers closer to end-users can minimize latency and improve performance while keeping costs in check.

Organizations with global operations must also consider compliance with data sovereignty laws, which can affect where data is stored. Providers often offer multi-region or geo-redundant storage solutions to address these issues, each impacting pricing differently.

### 6. Security and Compliance Considerations

Ensuring data protection and regulatory compliance requires additional features such as encryption, access controls, and audits, which often come at a premium. Organizations must evaluate the necessity and cost of these features based on the industry standards and regulations they are subject to.

Many cloud providers offer tiered security features, allowing organizations to select options aligned with their risk profiles and regulatory requirements. Investing in stringent security practices minimizes the risk of data breaches and compliance penalties, potentially reducing long-term financial impact.

## Cloud Storage Pricing Models

These are the most common pricing models offered by cloud storage providers:

### Subscription Pricing

Subscription pricing involves paying a fixed monthly or annual fee for a predefined amount of storage and associated services. This model offers predictable costs and is typically used by organizations with steady and consistent storage requirements. Providers may offer tiered subscription plans, allowing users to select the level of service that best aligns with their needs, such as storage capacity, data transfer limits, or additional features like advanced security.

This pricing model often comes with cost advantages through discounts for long-term commitments. However, it may not be ideal for organizations with fluctuating storage demands, as unused capacity still incurs costs. To maximize the value of subscription pricing, organizations should closely assess their current and projected storage needs to avoid underutilization or overpaying for unused resources.

### Pay-As-You-Go

The pay-as-you-go model charges users based on actual cloud storage usage, offering flexible scaling options. This model is advantageous for organizations with varying storage needs, as it avoids the commitment of upfront payments. However, unpredictable usage can lead to variegated monthly costs, potentially complicating budget management.

While it provides flexibility, pay-as-you-go may not always be the most cost-effective for stable, long-term projects. Organizations with consistent storage requirements might find reserved capacity options more economical in the long run.

### Reserved Capacity and Commitment Plans

Reserved capacity plans are for organizations with predictable usage patterns, offering a discounted rate by committing to a certain storage capacity over a specified period. This model suits organizations that can forecast their storage needs accurately, allowing them to maximize savings.

Committing to reserved plans can reduce costs significantly over time compared to pay-as-you-go models, but may limit flexibility in changing requirements. These plans require careful planning and resource allocation strategies to avoid penalty fees associated with underutilization.

✅ Pro Tip: With [N2W](/product), you can easily monitor AWS volume usage and set alerts for high or low usage.

### Tiered Storage Classes

Tiered storage classes address varying data access needs, optimizing costs by categorizing data based on frequency of access and retrieval patterns. Classes often include hot, cool, and cold tiers, each with its own cost implications. Hot storage is pricier due to fast access, suitable for frequently used data, while cool and cold storage are cost-effective for infrequent access.

Organizations benefit from cost savings by aligning data with the appropriate tier based on usage requirements. Implementing lifecycle policies that automatically transition data through tiers as it ages improves cost management.

* **Use multi-cloud strategies for pricing leverage**: Leverage multiple cloud providers to compare and negotiate better rates. Some providers may offer discounts for long-term or high-volume commitments when competition is apparent.
* **Implement cross-region replication selectively**: Only replicate critical data across regions to minimize storage and data transfer costs. Use geo-redundant storage sparingly for non-essential data to reduce unnecessary overhead.
* **Analyze access patterns with advanced monitoring**: Use tools like AWS CloudWatch, Azure Monitor, or third-party analytics platforms to track real-time data access trends. This helps fine-tune tier placement and avoid paying for underutilized resources.
* **Set up automated alerts for cost anomalies**: Configure alerts to notify the team of unexpected spikes in storage or egress costs. Early detection allows for quick troubleshooting and prevents budget overruns.
* **Use pre-signed URLs for efficiency**: Avoid overusing bandwidth for shared data by using pre-signed URLs to allow temporary, direct access to cloud objects, reducing unnecessary transfer fees.

* **Amazon Elastic Block Store (EBS):** Offers block storage volumes for use with Amazon EC2 instances, suitable for applications requiring low-latency access to data.

## 6 Cost Optimization Strategies for Cloud Storage

Organizations can optimize their storage costs in the cloud using the following practices.

### 1. Implementing Data Lifecycle Policies

Data lifecycle policies automate the transition of data through different storage tiers based on its age and access frequency. These policies ensure that data is retained cost-effectively, minimizing expenses associated with high-access storage. Automating data lifecycle management helps organizations reduce manual oversight and eliminate excessive costs.

By classifying data and setting rules for migration across storage classes, organizations can optimize resource use. Leveraging native cloud provider tools for implementing lifecycle policies simplifies the management process.

✅ Pro Tip: With N2W, you can automate lifecycle transitions, ensuring data is always stored in the most cost-efficient tier without requiring constant manual intervention.

### 2. Using Appropriate Storage Classes

Selecting suitable storage classes based on data access patterns is a key cost optimization strategy. Hot storage caters to high-access needs but incurs higher costs, while cool and cold storage offers lower-cost options for less frequent access.

By matching data to the appropriate storage class, organizations can efficiently balance performance needs with cost considerations. Using lifecycle management to transition data between storage classes as access patterns change further refines cost efficiency.

### 3. Data Compression and Deduplication

Implementing data compression and deduplication reduces storage footprints by minimizing redundant and repetitive data. Compression reduces the size of data, which translates to direct cost savings in storage. Deduplication removes duplicate data entries, potentially saving significant amounts of storage space, especially in environments with repetitive data patterns.

By using these techniques, organizations can improve data management without compromising on data integrity or accessibility. Employing built-in cloud provider tools or third-party solutions ensures data is stored in the most efficient way possible.

### 4. Archiving and Cold Storage Solutions

Archiving solutions provide cost-effective storage for infrequently accessed data. Cold storage, with its lower frequency and speed of access, offers the most budget-friendly solution for archival needs. This form of storage is suitable for long-term retention of data that does not require immediate access, saving significant storage costs over time.

Implementing strategies that differentiate between active and archived data helps organizations optimize their storage expenses. Using policies for automatic data archiving ensures that data is transferred to cost-efficient storage promptly.

### 5. Minimizing Data Egress Charges

Data egress charges are costs incurred when transferring data out of cloud storage solutions. These fees can become substantial, particularly with high-frequency data transfers. Minimizing egress costs involves strategic data management practices, such as reducing unnecessary data movement and optimizing data retrieval routes within available zones.

Employing geo-redundant solutions or using integrated data caching can help mitigate these charges. Additionally, organizations should evaluate providers that offer favorable egress terms to align with their data transfer needs.

### 6. Regularly Reviewing Storage Utilization

Regularly reviewing storage utilization involves frequent audits of current storage practices to identify inefficiencies and areas for optimization. Understanding where and how storage is used helps organizations eliminate unnecessary data, ensuring optimized resource use. Conducting these reviews systematically prevents waste and ensures alignment with business objectives.

Organizations benefit from using tools that offer detailed analytics, enabling informed decisions on data management practices. Shifting unnecessary or infrequently used data to more economical storage solutions aids in cost control.

✅ Pro Tip: N2W offers detailed analytics and reporting to help organizations identify unused data and optimize tiering, ensuring no storage resources are wasted.

## Frequently asked questions

****Q: How much does cloud storage cost across AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud?****

For standard, frequently accessed object storage, AWS S3 Standard is about $0.023 per GB-month for the first 50 TB, Azure Blob Hot is about $0.018 per GB-month, and Google Cloud Standard is about $0.020 per GB-month in its lower-cost regions. Cooler and archive tiers drop well below those rates. Region, redundancy, and request volume all change the final number.

****Q: Which cloud provider has the cheapest storage?****

It depends on the tier and region. For deep archive, Google Cloud Archive is among the lowest at roughly $0.0012 per GB-month in its cheapest regions. For standard hot storage, Azure Blob Hot tends to edge out AWS S3 and Google Cloud on the headline per-GB rate. The cheapest provider for your case depends on how often you read the data, how much you move out, and where it lives.

****Q: What are data egress charges?****

Egress charges are fees the provider applies when you move data out of its network, for example downloading backups or transferring between regions or clouds. Storing data is cheap, but moving it out can quietly become a large line item. You reduce egress by keeping restores in-region, caching frequently read data, and avoiding unnecessary cross-cloud transfers.

****Q: What factors affect cloud storage pricing beyond the per-GB rate?****

Several: the storage tier (hot, cool, archive), the redundancy and durability level, how often you read or retrieve data, request and operation counts, egress when data leaves the network, the region you store in, and any security or compliance requirements. Two workloads at the same per-GB rate can produce very different bills once retrievals and egress are counted.

****Q: How can I lower my cloud storage bill?****

Match each dataset to the right storage class, set lifecycle policies to move cold data to cheaper tiers automatically, compress and deduplicate before storing, archive old backups to cold tiers like S3 Glacier or Azure Archive, minimize cross-region and cross-cloud egress, and review usage regularly for orphaned data. For backup data specifically, N2W archives incrementally and reports up to 92% lower storage cost than standard snapshots.

### Storage Intelligence

Storage Intelligence

AI-powered [Storage Intelligence](https://cloud.google.com/storage/docs/storage-intelligence/overview) provides you with insights to help you manage and optimize storage at scale. Generate [storage insights datasets](https://cloud.google.com/storage/docs/insights/datasets) specific to your environment by querying object metadata & activity data at scale. Use [bucket relocation](https://cloud.google.com/storage/docs/bucket-relocation/overview) to minimize application downtime by automatically moving entire buckets while preserving their bucket names. Perform [batch operations](https://cloud.google.com/storage/docs/batch-operations/overview) at scale using managed jobs on millions of objects.

Storage Intelligence charges apply when configuring and using various capabilities as follows:

**Trial Tier**

The Storage Intelligence [30-day introductory trial](https://cloud.google.com/storage/docs/storage-intelligence/30-day-introductory-trial/overview) lets you learn and explore Storage Intelligence features and capabilities for up to 30 days. After activation, you can use features such as getting data insights with Gemini assistance, Storage Insights datasets, bucket relocation, and storage batch operations. The Storage Intelligence Object Management Fee is waived during the Trial period for the objects in scope of the trial & the Early Termination Fee does not apply during this period. Other charges as outlined below per feature will continue to apply. The Trial tier defaults to the Standard tier at the end of the 30-day period & charges associated with the Standard tier will begin to accrue.

**Standard Tier**

When configured for Standard tier the Storage Intelligence Standard Object Management Fee ($2.5 per million objects per month) applies to all objects within the specified Organization / Folder / Project. Unless filters are specified all buckets are included even as new ones are added. Any buckets that are removed from Standard Tier within 30 days of inclusion incur Storage Intelligence Early Termination Fee for the remaining duration. Charges are amortized daily and only apply to objects that exist more than 24 hours.

**Insights Datasets**

These can be configured for the same Organization / Folder / Project as the Storage Intelligence tier. When configured, daily snapshots are delivered for all the buckets/objects that have been enabled with Standard tier. Any number of Datasets can be configured for the same buckets and the Standard tier fee is only applied once.

BigQuery storage fees does apply for every instance for Datasets. Typically 1 TB of Cloud Storage data generates 300 MB of metadata daily however this can vary based on custom metadata stored within objects. Customers can configure the duration of snapshot retention. If Storage Intelligence is disabled for a project then new snapshots will not be delivered however the existing BigQuery data will not be deleted and will continue to incur storage charges. Customers can delete the Datasets configuration at any time to remove their data from BigQuery.

**Note:** Active Logical Storage charges in BigQuery will be waived for 90 days after the GA launch date for the data stored in the following new views: object\_events\_view, bucket\_activity\_view, project\_activity\_view, and bucket\_region\_activity\_view. After this 90-day promotional period post the GA launch, standard BigQuery storage fees will be charged for these views. All other BigQuery storage remains subject to standard charges.

**Note:** This will not impact the active logical storage charges for existing metadata tables (bucket\_attributes\_latest\_snapshot\_view, bucket\_attributes\_view, error\_attributes\_view, events\_view, object\_attributes\_latest\_snapshot\_view, object\_attributes\_view, project\_attributes\_view) which will continue to accrue active logical storage costs.

Rapid Cache

The following pricing applies to any bucket where Rapid Cache is enabled. Rapid Cache pricing is supplemental to the overall service pricing. Unless explicitly stated, the Cloud Storage service prices provided elsewhere in this document continue to apply in addition to Rapid Cache prices.

When reading data that is not already cached in the same zone where the data is being read, all normal Cloud Storage prices apply for the request (for example: Class B operations and multi-region data transfer out charges). When the data being read in a particular zone is already cached in that zone’s cache, cache operations charges apply for requests instead of the normal higher priced Class B operations. Cache data transfer out charges are also assessed based on the volume of data read.

## Google Cloud Storage Pricing Overview

This document details pricing for Google Cloud Storage (not Google Drive). Pricing is based on components including data storage, data processing, operation charges, retrieval fees, network usage, and additional features. Prices are listed in USD; other currencies shown on Cloud Platform SKUs apply.

### Data Storage
Storage is charged per gibibyte-hour, prorated to the sub-second. Storage classes include Standard, Nearline, Coldline, Archive, and Rapid Cache/Rapid Storage, with varying costs depending on location type (Region, Dual-region, Multi-region, Zonal).

**Region pricing (per GiB/hour):**
- Standard: $0.000027397 (~$0.020/GB/month)
- Nearline: $0.000013699 (~$0.010/GB/month)
- Coldline: $0.000005479 (~$0.004/GB/month)
- Archive: $0.000001644 (~$0.0012/GB/month)
- Rapid Cache: $0.0001233

**Minimum storage durations:** Nearline (30 days), Coldline (90 days), Archive (365 days). Early deletion incurs charges as if stored for the minimum duration.

### Operation Charges
Operations are categorized as Class A, Class B, Class C, Class D, or Free. Costs vary by storage class, location type, and namespace (flat vs. hierarchical). For example, in a single region with Standard storage: Class A operations cost $0.005/1,000 operations (flat) or $0.0065 (hierarchical); Class B operations cost $0.0004/1,000 (flat) or $0.0005 (hierarchical).

### Retrieval Fees
Applied when reading data from Nearline ($0.01/GiB), Coldline ($0.02/GiB), or Archive ($0.05/GiB). No retrieval fees for Standard, Rapid, or Autoclass-enabled buckets.

### Network/Data Transfer
- **Within Google Cloud:** Free within same location. Between regions, costs range from $0.02/GiB (within Northern America or Europe) to $0.14/GiB (to Latin America).
- **General (internet) usage:** Free inbound. Outbound to worldwide destinations: $0.12/GB (0-10 TiB), $0.11/GB (10-150 TiB), $0.08/GB (150+ TiB). Higher rates for China and Australia.

### Autoclass
Management fee of $0.0025 per 1,000 objects per 30 days. One-time enablement charge for reclassifying existing objects.

### Storage Intelligence
Standard tier: $2.5 per million objects per month. 30-day trial tier available. Early termination fee applies if removed within 30 days.

### Other Features
- **Tags:** $0.005 per tag per month
- **Inventory Reports:** $0.0025-$0.0028 per million objects
- **Rapid Cache:** Cache ingest ($0.0032/GiB), cache operations ($0.0002/1,000), cache data transfer out ($0.0006/GiB). Cache storage per Rapid Cache rates above.
- **Rapid Bucket (zonal):** Data transfer out ($0.0006/GiB), data transfer in ($0.0032/GiB). Storage per Rapid storage rates.
- **Object Contexts:** $3 per million objects per month
- **Bucket Relocation:** $0.04/GB for data moved, plus applicable charges per source/destination matrix.

### Always Free Tier (US-WEST1, US-CENTRAL1, US-EAST1 only)
- 5 GB-months of Standard storage
- 5,000 Class A operations
- 50,000 Class B operations
- 100 GB data transfer from North America (excluding Australia/China)

# Oracle Pricing 2026: Plans, Costs & What You'll Actually Pay

[Oracle](https://checkthat.ai/brands/oracle) transitioned from perpetual licensing to subscription and credit-based consumption models, but the shift didn't clarify pricing. Unlike AWS or Azure, Oracle doesn't publish list prices for most enterprise deals. Every significant purchase requires direct sales engagement, and the gap between published rates and negotiated prices can exceed 50%.

This guide decodes what you'll actually pay across Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI), Autonomous Database, and Fusion Cloud applications, including the hidden costs and negotiation leverage points that Oracle's marketing materials won't mention.

## [Copied to clipboardTL;DR: Oracle Pricing At a Glance](#tldr-oracle-pricing-at-a-glance)

Oracle's primary pricing models and their best-fit scenarios:

| Plan/Model | Pricing Approach | Best For | Key Features |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| OCI Pay-As-You-Go | Monthly billing, no commitment | Testing, POCs, variable workloads | No upfront cost, list-price rates, full flexibility |
| OCI Annual Commitment | Universal Credits, 1–3 year terms | Production workloads, predictable demand | Volume discounts available (specific percentages not published), credit pooling |
| Always Free Tier | Perpetual free resources | Learning, development, small workloads | 2 Autonomous DBs, 4 ARM OCPUs, 200GB storage |
| Autonomous Database (License Included) | Per-ECPU/hour with license bundled | Greenfield projects, no existing Oracle licenses | Fully managed, auto-patching, higher hourly rates |
| Autonomous Database (BYOL) | Per-ECPU/hour, bring your license | Existing Database EE customers | 76% discount vs. License Included |
| Fusion Cloud ERP | Per-user/month subscription | Mid-market to enterprise finance/supply chain | 3-year minimum, 40-user minimum for Core ERP (alternative 10-user SKU exists) |
| Fusion Cloud HCM | Per-employee/month subscription | Enterprise HR operations | 500-employee minimum for most modules |

## [Copied to clipboardWhat You Actually Pay](#what-you-actually-pay)

Oracle operates a quote-based pricing model for enterprise deals. While per-unit rates appear on pricing pages, actual costs depend heavily on commitment size, existing license portfolio, and negotiation timing.

> "Oracle does not publish standard list prices for enterprise agreements. All significant pricing requires direct sales engagement. Budget planning should account for 30–60% discount potential on multi-year commitments, but starting point varies significantly by workload and negotiating power."

### [Copied to clipboardUniversal Credits: Annual Commitment vs. PAYG](#universal-credits-annual-commitment-vs-payg)

Oracle's Universal Credits model offers two primary paths:

* **Pay-As-You-Go (PAYG):** No upfront commitment, billed monthly in arrears at list price. Maximum flexibility, but you pay the highest per-unit rates.
* **Annual Universal Credits:** Commit to a minimum annual spend ($2,000 minimum, $100,000 for volume discounts) and receive discounted rates. One-to-three-year terms available, with deeper discounts for longer commitments.

The discount structure isn't published, but [market benchmarks](https://redresscompliance.com/oracle-oci-pricing-universal-credits-guide.html) suggest the following ranges:

| Annual Commitment | Typical Discount vs. PAYG |
| --- | --- |
| $100K–$500K | 10–15% |
| $500K–$2M | 15–25% |
| $2M–$5M | 25–35% |
| $5M+ | 33%+ for strategic accounts |

These represent market benchmarks; actual negotiated discounts vary by customer leverage, timing, and bundled commitments. Three-year terms typically outperform one-year by 8–12% in discount depth. However, unused credits don't roll over: they expire at term end. Organizations with unpredictable consumption patterns must account for this expiration risk when sizing commitments. For monthly flex commitments, unused monthly credits are forfeited at month-end.

### [Copied to clipboardBYOL: Reducing Hourly Rates by 76%](#byol-reducing-hourly-rates-by-76)

If you hold existing Oracle Database Enterprise Edition licenses, Bring Your Own License (BYOL) delivers the single largest cost reduction available. BYOL [reduces Autonomous Database compute costs by 76%](https://blogs.oracle.com/cloud-infrastructure/post/license-investment-byol-autonomous-database) compared to License Included pricing.

BYOL eligibility requirements:

* **Eligible workloads:** Transaction Processing and Lakehouse only (JSON Database and APEX are excluded)
* **License types:** Full Use, Limited Use, Application Specific Full Use, Proprietary Hosting, ULA-covered, or perpetual/term licenses with active support
* **Conversion ratio:** 1 processor license (or 25 Named User Plus) covers 8 ECPUs or 2 OCPUs

For a 128-OCPU Oracle Database EE instance, BYOL can translate to approximately $2.4M in annual compute cost savings versus License Included pricing, based on the 76% reduction in compute costs that BYOL provides compared to License Included.

### [Copied to clipboardSupport Rewards: Offset On-Premises Support Bills](#support-rewards-offset-on-premises-support-bills)

Oracle's Support Rewards program converts OCI spending into credits against on-premises support invoices at rates of $0.25–$0.33 per $1 spent on OCI, depending on customer type:

| Customer Type | Credit Rate |
| --- | --- |
| Standard (non-ULA) | $0.25 per $1.00 OCI spend |
| Unlimited License Agreement holders | $0.33 per $1.00 OCI spend |

For a large enterprise spending $4M annually on OCI under a ULA, the 33% rate generates $1.32M in annual credits, potentially eliminating on-premises support costs entirely. However, rewards expire 12 months from issuance and cannot be applied retroactively to invoices with passed due dates. Oracle SaaS subscriptions (Fusion Cloud ERP/HCM) are explicitly excluded from earning rewards.

### [Copied to clipboardAlways Free Tier: What's Actually Included](#always-free-tier-whats-actually-included)

Oracle's Always Free Tier provides perpetual access to limited resources without a credit card:

* **Compute:** 2 AMD VMs (1/8 OCPU each) + 4 ARM Ampere OCPUs with 24GB RAM
* **Autonomous Databases:** 2 instances, 20GB storage each
* **Storage:** 200GB block volume + 20GB object storage
* **Networking:** 10TB outbound data transfer monthly

These resources are permanent and don't require upgrading to a paid account. However, they're limited to home-region availability and are not suitable for production enterprise workloads.

### [Copied to clipboardFusion Cloud Minimums: Seat Packs and Thresholds](#fusion-cloud-minimums-seat-packs-and-thresholds)

Enterprise SaaS pricing carries minimum seat requirements that can surprise organizations during procurement:

| Module | Minimum Seats | List Price (Monthly) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Fusion ERP Core | 40 users (B108685) or 10 users (B91079) | $625/user |
| Fusion Procurement | 10 users | $625/user |
| Fusion Talent Management | 500 users | $7/user |
| Fusion Payroll (US) | 500 employees | $8/employee |
| Fusion Learning | 500 users | $5/user |

**Note:** Two separate Fusion ERP Core SKUs exist with different minimums (B108685: 40-user minimum; B91079: 10-user minimum). Consult Oracle Sales to determine eligibility.

All Fusion Cloud subscriptions require a [3-year minimum term](https://www.oracle.com/a/ocom/docs/corporate/pricing/oracle-fusion-cloud-global-price-list.pdf). Negotiated discounts typically run 40–60% off list, yielding effective rates of approximately $175–$450/user/month depending on module and volume.

## [Copied to clipboardWhat Drives Your Costs](#what-drives-your-costs)

Understanding Oracle's cost drivers helps you model accurate budgets before engaging sales. The primary factors differ significantly between OCI infrastructure and Fusion Cloud applications.

### [Copied to clipboardOCPU vs. vCPU: The Unit That Matters](#ocpu-vs-vcpu-the-unit-that-matters)

Oracle's CPU pricing uses OCPUs (Oracle CPUs), not vCPUs. This distinction materially affects cost comparisons:

| Unit | Physical Cores | Hyperthreads |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 OCI OCPU (x86) | 1 | 2 |
| 1 AWS vCPU | 0.5 | 1 |
| 1 Azure vCPU | 0.5 | 1 |

One OCPU equals two vCPUs on AWS or Azure. When Oracle's per-OCPU price appears higher than a competitor's per-vCPU price, the actual cost-per-compute-thread is often lower. OCI compute [costs roughly half as much as AWS](https://blogs.oracle.com/cloud-infrastructure/post/vcpu-and-ocpu-pricing-information) for equivalent workloads when comparing per-vCPU pricing.

### [Copied to clipboardCompute Tier Options](#compute-tier-options)

OCI offers multiple compute shapes with different price-performance characteristics:

* **VM Standard:** Flexible shapes (E5, E6) for general-purpose workloads; configure OCPU and memory independently
* **VM Optimized:** Dense I/O shapes for storage-intensive applications
* **Bare Metal:** Dedicated physical servers (up to 256 OCPUs, 3TB RAM on E6 shapes) for maximum performance and licensing simplicity
* **Preemptible Instances:** 50% of regular instance pricing for fault-tolerant, interruptible workloads

Specific per-OCPU rates vary by shape and load dynamically on Oracle's pricing pages. Use the [OCI Cost Estimator](https://www.oracle.com/cloud/costestimator.html) for current rates on your specific configuration.

### [Copied to clipboardStorage Tiers and Performance Costs](#storage-tiers-and-performance-costs)

Block Volume pricing depends on both capacity and performance tier:

| VPU Level | Performance Tier | $/VPU/GB/month |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | Lower Cost | $0.000 |
| 10 | Balanced | $0.017 |
| 20 | Higher Performance | $0.034 |
| 30–100 | Ultra High Performance | $0.051–$0.170 |

Object Storage and Archive Storage follow standard per-GB/month models, with Archive Storage running approximately $0.0026/GB/month in most regions.

### [Copied to clipboardData Egress: Oracle's Major Cost Advantage](#data-egress-oracles-major-cost-advantage)

OCI includes [10TB of free outbound data transfer monthly](https://www.oracle.com/cloud/networking/networking-pricing.html), 100× more than AWS or Azure's 100GB free tier. Beyond the free allowance, OCI charges approximately $0.0085/GB versus AWS's $0.09/GB.

For data-egress-heavy workloads, this difference compounds dramatically:

| Monthly Egress | OCI Cost | AWS Cost | Azure Cost |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 10TB | $0 | ~$819 | ~$788 |
| 50TB | ~$425 | ~$4,419 | ~$4,188 |
| 100TB | ~$850 | ~$7,691 | ~$7,588 |

Organizations streaming video, distributing large datasets, or running IoT analytics should weight egress costs heavily in TCO calculations.

### [Copied to clipboardAutonomous Database Consumption](#autonomous-database-consumption)

Autonomous Database bills on three dimensions:

* **ECPU hours:** Compute consumption, auto-scaled unless thresholds are configured
* **Storage:** Per-GB/month for data and backups
* **Backup retention:** Extended retention periods incur additional storage costs

Auto-scaling can spike costs unexpectedly if maximum ECPU thresholds aren't configured. The database automatically scales up during peak demand, beneficial for performance but potentially expensive if uncapped.

### [Copied to clipboardFusion Cloud: Beyond Per-User Fees](#fusion-cloud-beyond-per-user-fees)

Fusion Cloud ERP and HCM subscription costs represent only a fraction of total deployment expense. Implementation and ongoing costs typically include:

* **System integrator fees:** $800K–$9M+ depending on scope
* **Data migration:** $100K–$2M depending on complexity
* **Training and change management:** Often underbudgeted
* **Quarterly upgrade testing:** Mandatory SaaS updates require continuous resource allocation for testing and managing internal changes every three months

A [Gartner Peer Insights reviewer](https://www.gartner.com/reviews/market/cloud-erp-for-product-centric-enterprises/vendor/oracle/product/oracle-fusion-cloud-erp/reviews?reviewFilter=pricing) flagged this as a common frustration: "Mandatory Quarterly Testing – Constant SaaS upgrades require continuous resource allocation for testing and managing internal changes every three months."

## [Copied to clipboardWhat You Get At Each Tier](#what-you-get-at-each-tier)

Oracle's offerings span infrastructure, database, and enterprise applications. Each tier serves different organizational needs and carries distinct cost structures.

### [Copied to clipboardOracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI): PAYG](#oracle-cloud-infrastructure-oci-payg)

**Overview:** Hourly, per-resource billing with no upfront commitment. Resources are charged at Oracle's published list rates, billed monthly in arrears.

**Best for:** Startups testing Oracle workloads, proof-of-concept projects, variable or unpredictable demand patterns, and organizations unwilling to commit capital upfront.

**What's included:**

* Full access to OCI compute, storage, and networking services
* 10TB free monthly egress
* Enterprise-ready support included in base fees
* Always Free Tier resources (2 VMs, 2 Autonomous DBs, 200GB storage)

**Verdict:** PAYG works well for exploration and variable workloads but becomes expensive at scale. Organizations with predictable demand should evaluate Annual Commitment for 20–60% savings.

### [Copied to clipboardOracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI): Annual Commitment](#oracle-cloud-infrastructure-oci-annual-commitment)

**Overview:** Universal Credits with 1–3 year terms. Commit to an annual spend minimum and receive discounted consumption rates across all OCI services.

**Best for:** Production workloads, organizations with 12+ months of predictable demand, teams requiring budget certainty, and enterprises migrating significant on-premises infrastructure.

**What's included:**

* Discounted per-unit rates (10–35% below PAYG depending on commitment size)
* Credit pooling across services and regions
* Overage charged at contracted rate card (not list price)
* Support Rewards eligibility ($0.25–$0.33 per dollar spent)

**Verdict:** Annual Commitment delivers meaningful savings for predictable workloads. Negotiate overage rates explicitly; without protection, excess usage above committed amount is invoiced monthly in arrears at the contracted rate card, not list price.

### [Copied to clipboardAutonomous Database: License Included](#autonomous-database-license-included)

**Overview:** Fully managed Oracle Database with Enterprise Edition licensing bundled into hourly ECPU charges. No existing Oracle licenses required.

**Best for:** Greenfield projects, organizations without existing Oracle Database licenses, and teams prioritizing operational simplicity over cost optimization.

**What's included:**

* ECPU allocation with auto-scaling
* Storage and automated backups
* Automatic patching and updates
* Full Oracle Database Enterprise Edition capabilities

**Limitations:** Higher hourly rates than BYOL. Organizations with existing Oracle licenses may not fully leverage the BYOL discount of 76% on Autonomous Database compute costs.

**Verdict:** License Included simplifies procurement for new Oracle customers but carries a substantial premium. Calculate the crossover point against BYOL if you have any existing Oracle Database entitlements.

### [Copied to clipboardAutonomous Database: BYOL](#autonomous-database-byol)

**Overview:** Bring your existing Oracle Database licenses to Autonomous Database and receive a 76% discount on compute costs.

**Best for:** Organizations with existing Oracle Database Enterprise Edition licenses under active support, particularly those with ULA agreements or significant perpetual license portfolios.

**What's included:**

* 76% reduction in ECPU hourly rates versus License Included
* Same managed service capabilities (auto-patching, auto-scaling)
* License conversion at 1 processor = 8 ECPUs

**Verdict:** BYOL represents the optimal path for existing Oracle Database customers. The 76% savings can translate to millions annually for large database footprints. However, only Transaction Processing and Lakehouse workloads qualify; JSON Database and APEX require License Included.

### [Copied to clipboardFusion Cloud ERP](#fusion-cloud-erp)

**Overview:** Per-user subscription model for enterprise finance, procurement, and supply chain management. Standard 3-year minimum term.

**Best for:** Enterprise organizations ($500M+ revenue, 5,000+ employees) requiring unified financial management, procurement automation, and supply chain visibility.

**What's included:**

* Core modules: Financial Management, Procurement, Supply Chain
* Quarterly feature updates (mandatory)
* Cloud-native architecture with Oracle's infrastructure

**What's NOT included:**

* Implementation services ($800K–$9M+ depending on scope)
* Data migration ($100K–$2M)
* Training and change management
* Post-go-live support beyond standard SLA

**Verdict:** Fusion Cloud ERP delivers comprehensive functionality but total cost of ownership extends well beyond subscription fees. [ERPResearch.com estimates](https://www.erpresearch.com/blog/en-us/blog/oracle-erp-cloud-implementation-cost-breakdown) Year 1 total costs of $3.6M–$5.6M for a 500-user mid-market organization, with implementation services often exceeding software costs.

### [Copied to clipboardFusion Cloud HCM](#fusion-cloud-hcm)

**Overview:** Per-employee subscription for HR, payroll, talent management, and workforce planning.

**Best for:** Enterprise HR operations (5,000+ employees) requiring unified human capital management with global payroll capabilities.

**What's included:**

* Core HR and organizational management
* Payroll processing (country-specific modules priced separately)
* Talent management: recruiting, learning, performance
* Workforce compensation and benefits administration

**Verdict:** Fusion Cloud HCM scales well for large enterprises but carries high minimum seat requirements (500+ for most modules, 500 for US Payroll). Mid-market organizations may find the minimums prohibitive.

### [Copied to clipboardAlways Free Tier](#always-free-tier)

**Overview:** Perpetual free access to limited OCI resources. No credit card required, no time limit.

**Best for:** Learning Oracle Cloud, development environments, small production workloads that fit within resource caps.

**What's included:**

* 2 AMD VMs (1/8 OCPU each)
* 4 ARM Ampere A1 OCPU-hours with 24GB RAM
* 2 Autonomous Databases (20GB each)
* 200GB block volume + 20GB object storage
* 10TB monthly egress

**Limitations:** Resources are capped and home-region only. Cannot support enterprise production workloads.

**Verdict:** Valuable for experimentation and learning. The 2 Autonomous Databases provide genuine utility for development and testing scenarios.

Oracle's published rates serve as negotiation starting points, not final prices. Several factors improve your leverage:

## [Copied to clipboardIs Oracle Worth It?](#is-oracle-worth-it)

Oracle's value proposition depends heavily on your existing technology stack, workload characteristics, and organizational constraints.

### [Copied to clipboardWhen Oracle Delivers Clear ROI](#when-oracle-delivers-clear-roi)

**Compute performance:** OCI's bare metal offerings and OCPU efficiency create genuine cost-per-performance advantages. Phoronix's October 2025 benchmark tested OCI E6 across 130+ workloads against equivalent-spec instances from AWS, Azure, and GCP, finding that the OCI E6 8 OCPU instance (16 vCPUs) ["came out ahead of the other 16 vCPU instances tested across the Microsoft Azure, Google Cloud, and Amazon AWS public clouds."](https://www.phoronix.com/review/oracle-e6-amd-epyc-cloud/7) The benchmark also noted that "for CPU-based AI inferencing options, Oracle E6 was performing incredibly well there and by far the best value of the tested instance types."

**Data egress savings:** For organizations moving 50TB+ monthly, OCI's 10TB free allowance and $0.0085/GB overage rate saves approximately $7,000/month versus AWS or Azure ($84,000+ annually).

**Database licensing simplification:** BYOL eliminates audit risk, SAM complexity, and support negotiation friction for existing Oracle Database customers. The 76% compute discount compounds into millions for large database footprints.

**Existing Oracle ecosystem:** Organizations with significant Oracle investments (Database, Middleware, Applications) can leverage BYOL and Support Rewards to reduce total Oracle spending while modernizing infrastructure.

### [Copied to clipboardWhen Oracle Is NOT Worth It](#when-oracle-is-not-worth-it)

**Budget constraints:** Fusion Cloud's minimum seat requirements (40+ for ERP Core, 500+ for HCM modules) and 3-year terms create substantial upfront commitments. Mid-market organizations may find alternatives more accessible.

**Lack of Oracle expertise:** Oracle's ecosystem rewards deep familiarity. Organizations without existing Oracle skills face steeper learning curves and higher implementation risk.

**Preference for rapid deployment:** Fusion Cloud ERP implementations typically span 12–24 months, with 55% of organizations completing full implementations in 2 years according to [Gartner](https://checkthat.ai/brands/gartner) Peer Community data. Organizations prioritizing speed-to-value may find cloud-native alternatives faster to deploy.

**Open-source database preference:** If you're running PostgreSQL, MySQL, or other open-source databases, OCI's managed database pricing advantage (approximately 44% cheaper than AWS RDS) doesn't require Oracle's broader ecosystem.

**Implementation cost sensitivity:** Fusion Cloud ERP/HCM projects typically require 6–18 months and $700K–$9M+ in consulting and training. [Edinburgh University's implementation](https://panorama-consulting.com/edinburgh-universitys-failed-implementation/) contracted at £25M and rose to £37M (a 48% overrun). Implementation costs frequently exceed software subscription costs, with total Year 1 costs for mid-market organizations (500 users) ranging from $3.6M–$5.6M including software, implementation, internal staff, and integration.

### [Copied to clipboardBottom Line](#bottom-line)

Oracle offers competitive infrastructure pricing and best-in-class SaaS applications for organizations already invested in the Oracle ecosystem. BYOL delivers transformative savings for existing Database customers, reducing compute costs by 76% compared to License Included pricing for eligible Transaction Processing and Lakehouse workloads. OCI's 10 TB free monthly egress creates genuine advantages for data-intensive workloads, with overage rates of $0.0085/GB compared to AWS at $0.09/GB and Azure at $0.087/GB.

However, Oracle's pricing opacity, minimum commitment requirements, and implementation complexity create barriers for price-sensitive or smaller organizations. The gap between Oracle's marketing claims (50–80% savings) and independent analysis (7.7% TCO advantage in the only audited study) warrants skepticism.

For enterprise decision-makers: model your specific workloads using Oracle's [Cost Estimator](https://www.oracle.com/cloud/costestimator.html), factor in your existing license portfolio, and negotiate aggressively, especially during Oracle's fiscal Q4 (February–May, fiscal year ends May 31).

This webpage from Checkthat.ai provides a comprehensive guide to Oracle pricing in 2026, covering Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI), Autonomous Database, and Fusion Cloud applications. The key takeaway is that Oracle has transitioned from perpetual licensing to subscription and credit-based consumption models, but pricing remains opaque—most enterprise deals require direct sales engagement, and negotiated discounts can reach 50%+ off list prices.

**Pricing Models Overview:**
- **OCI Pay-As-You-Go:** Monthly billing, no commitment, highest rates
- **OCI Annual Commitment (Universal Credits):** 1–3 year terms with 10–35% discounts vs. PAYG depending on commitment size ($100K–$5M+)
- **Always Free Tier:** Perpetual free resources (2 Autonomous DBs, 4 ARM OCPUs, 200GB storage, 10TB egress)
- **Autonomous Database (License Included):** Per-ECPU/hour with license bundled
- **Autonomous Database (BYOL):** 76% discount vs. License Included for existing Oracle Database EE customers
- **Fusion Cloud ERP/HCM:** Per-user/month subscriptions, 3-year minimum terms, with minimum seat requirements (40 for ERP Core, 500 for HCM modules)

**Key Cost Drivers:**
- OCPUs (Oracle CPUs) = 2 vCPUs, making OCI's per-thread pricing often lower than AWS/Azure
- OCI includes 10TB free monthly egress (100x more than AWS/Azure), with overage at $0.0085/GB vs. AWS $0.09/GB
- Support Rewards program converts OCI spending to credits against on-premises support at $0.25–$0.33 per $1 spent
- Unused Universal Credits expire at term end

**Competitive Comparison:**
- OCI compute is 35–60% cheaper than AWS for equivalent configurations
- Only independent 3-year TCO study found just 7.7% advantage for Oracle in BYOL scenario (contradicting Oracle's 50–80% marketing claims)
- Fusion Cloud ERP: $625/user/month list, negotiated to $175–$450; implementations cost $800K–$9M+

**Bottom Line:** Oracle delivers competitive infrastructure pricing and strong SaaS for existing Oracle customers, especially via BYOL (76% savings) and Support Rewards. However, pricing opacity, minimum commitments, and implementation complexity create barriers. The gap between Oracle's marketing claims and independent analysis warrants skepticism. Best negotiation leverage occurs during Oracle's fiscal Q4 (February–May).

# Archive Storage FAQs

**FAQ topics**

## General

### What is Oracle Cloud Infrastructure Archive Storage?

Oracle Cloud Infrastructure Archive Storage is a storage tier ideal for storing long living data that is accessed infrequently. Data stored in Oracle Archive Storage can be accessed using the same interfaces as the Oracle Object Storage (API, SDK, CLI), however unlike Oracle Object Storage, data retrieval is not instantaneous. You need to restore data from the archive storage before it can be read. From the time a restore request is made, it takes at most an hour to read the data. This time is measured as Time To First Byte (TTFB). You can achieve WORM compliance with Oracle Archive Storage by leveraging Retention Rules to manage data access.

### What use cases does the Oracle Archive Storage address?

Oracle Archive Storage addresses the following use cases:

**Backup/Archive:**

Backup/archive data often needs to be stored for a extended duration to adhere to various compliance mandates. Once created, this backup/archive data is rarely accessed. Archive Storage is the appropriate tier to store this data.

**Log Data:**

You may need to preserve your application log data to retroactively analyze this data to determine usage pattern and/or debug issues. Because log data is typically not accessed unless required, the Archive Storage tier provides a cost efficient way to preserve and store this data.

**Content Preservation:**

Preserving a large amount of rich media content (images, videos, etc.) on traditional storage can get expensive quickly. If you have content that you need to preserve, but do not access that content frequently, Archive Storage is the perfect tier to store this data.

**Very Large Data Sets:**

If your applications generate a large amount of data (genome data, pharmaceutical trials data, IOT data, etc.) that needs to be preserved for future use, Archive Storage is the appropriate tier to store this data. The inherent cost efficiency of Archive Storage offsets the long lead time required to access the data.

### How are the Oracle Object Storage and Archive Storage tiers differentiated?

|  | Object Storage | Archive Storage |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Minimum Duration to Store Objects** | N/A | 90 Days |
| **Storage Cost** | US$0.0255 / GB (First 10 GB/month free) | US$0.0026 / GB\* (First 10 GB/month free) |
| **Request Cost** | US$0.0034 / 10K Requests | US$0.0034 / 10K Requests |
| **Bandwidth Cost** | US$0.0085 / GB (First 10 TB/month free) | US$0.0085 / GB (First 10 TB/month free) |

\*If you delete data from Archive Storage before the minimum retention requirements are met, you are charged a deletion penalty. The deletion penalty is the prorated cost of storing the data for the full 90 days.

| --- | --- | --- |
| **Minimum Duration to Store Objects** | N/A | 90 Days |
| **Storage Cost** | US$0.0255 / GB (First 10 GB/month free) | US$0.0026 / GB\* (First 10 GB/month free) |
| **Request Cost** | US$0.0034 / 10K Requests | US$0.0034 / 10K Requests |
| **Bandwidth Cost** | US$0.0085 / GB (First 10 TB/month free) | US$0.0085 / GB (First 10 TB/month free) |

\*If you delete data from Archive Storage before the minimum retention requirements are met, you are charged a deletion penalty. The deletion penalty is the prorated cost of storing the data for the full 90 days.

### How do I choose the storage tier I want to store my data on?

The storage tier is expressed as a property of the bucket when the bucket is created. By default, all new objects inherit the storage property of the bucket. Once set, the bucket storage property cannot be modified. An existing standard Object Storage bucket cannot be downgraded to Archive Storage tier and an Archive Storage bucket cannot be upgraded to the standard Object Storage tier.

### an I apply the storage tier property to specific objects in a bucket instead of the entire bucket?

No, the storage tier property cannot be applied to a specific object or an object group. Storage tiers can only be expressed as a property of the bucket. All objects automatically inherit the storage tier property of the bucket to which they belong.

### Which APIs can I use to manage Archive Storage data?

You use the existing Oracle Object Storage APIs to manage Archive Storage data. In addition, Oracle Archive Storage supports a 'Restore' API to restore the archived data, so that it can be read.

### How do I retrieve data from Archive Storage?

To retrieve data from the Archive Storage tier, you first need restore the data to Object Storage. After the data is restored, you have a window of time to download the data.

By default you have 24 hours to download data once it's restored, but you can alternatively specify a download time of from 1 to 240 hours. After the download time expires, the data automatically returns to its previously archived state.

To retrieve data from the Archive Storage tier, you first need restore the data to Object Storage. After the data is restored, you have a window of time to download the data.

By default you have 24 hours to download data once it's restored, but you can alternatively specify a download time of from 1 to 240 hours. After the download time expires, the data automatically returns to its previously archived state.

### How long does it take to restore data from Archive Storage after a restore request is made?

From the time a restore request is made, it takes at most an hour to read the data. This time is measured as Time To First Byte (TTFB).

### Can I customize the duration time for which the restored data is accessible for download on the Object Storage tier?

You can specify a duration time from 1 to 240 hours that the restored data is accessible for download on the Object Storage tier. If you do not explicitly set a duration time, data is available for download for 24 hours by default.

### Can I restore archived data, by specifying object prefixes?

No, you cannot restore data by selecting object prefixes.

### Can I access archived object's metadata when the object is in its archived state?

Yes, you can always access archived object's metadata, regardless of whether the object is in an archived or restored state.

### Is there a minimum size requirement for storing data in the Archive Storage tier?

No, there are no minimum size requirements to store data in the Archive Storage.

### Is the Archive Storage tier WORM compliant?

Yes, Oracle Archive Storage is WORM compliant. This is achieved by leveraging Retention Rules to prevent data from being deleted or overwritten. Retention Rules can be locked to prevent rule modification and data deletion or modification even by administrators.

### Will the Archive Storage tier match the durability and availability characteristics of the standard Object Storage tier?

Yes, Archive Storage matches the durability and availability characteristics of standard Object Storage.

After the window expires, data returns to its archived state. Restore operations cannot be done by object prefix.

- **Metadata**: Object metadata is always accessible, even when the object is archived.

# Oracle Cloud Infrastructure: Features & Price

Oracle Cloud Infrastructure includes block, file, object, and archive storage services. Discover its features, uses, security and more. Click here now.

Written By [![](data:image/avif;base64,)
![Drew Robb](https://cdn.enterprisestorageforum.com/571f5f9e2ff5f3cf9c75063e22ff3e09.png?w=64)

## Bottom Line:

Oracle is generally seen as a niche player for [cloud storage](https://www.enterprisestorageforum.com/management/survey-results-cloud-storage-takes-off-flash-cools-off/). In general market profile, it runs ahead of IBM, Virtustream and Rackspace, but clearly behind cloud storage market leaders AWS and Azure.

Oracle gets high marks for its full menu of cloud storage features. Enterprise buyers will find a robust offering that serves all of their workload needs.

Oracle’s historic strength, of course, is in the database business. So, unsurprisingly, Oracle’s OCI Classic offering is suited to users of traditional Oracle databases and applications. In contrast, OCI is more suited to users with cloud-native applications and batch computing requirements that benefit from bare-metal servers. This cloud-native offering is forward looking on Oracle’s part.

Oracle offers high performance at a price that’s compelling, given overall [cloud storage pricing](https://www.enterprisestorageforum.com/cloud/cloud-storage-pricing/). Still, because the company has historically been so focused on its own platform, the storage service is probably best for those already using Oracle databases and applications.

## Company Description:

Oracle is a well-established provider of enterprise IT services across a range of software and hardware products. It began in databases, expanded into enterprise software and now offers a wide range of cloud-based offerings. Customers include Gonzaga University, Allianz, National Grid. Rolls-Royce, and Office Depot.

## Service Description:

Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) was launched in 2016. It includes block, file, object, and archive storage services. It provides a full range of storage offerings aimed at satisfying the demanding needs of enterprise and software vendor users across systems of record and cloud native workloads.

The offerings are designed to be simple enough to deploy with few tiers of service, and predictable in cost with low rates that include all performance. Its storage utilizes [nonvolatile memory express](https://www.enterprisestorageforum.com/hardware/nmve/) (NVMe) and [SSD-based storage](https://www.enterprisestorageforum.com/hardware/benefits-of-ssd-speed-and-performance/) to boost performance.

Advertisement

## Storage Type:

Block, file, and object.

## Locations:

OCI operates storage services in data centers in the U.S., U.K. and Germany.

## Differentiator:

Oracle offers the highest performance [block storage](https://www.enterprisestorageforum.com/hardware/block-storage/) in the industry with 60 IOPS/GB, and all that performance is included in the low base price. File storage has the same pricing as block storage, which makes this service cost less than comparable offerings from competitors. All storage is SSD backed.

“The sales and technology teams have been outstanding. We’ve had multiple on-site meetings with prospects and customers, which included Oracle staff, and that has made a significant difference in our speed to market and prospect comfort levels,” said a marketing manager in the transportation industry.

## Implementation:

Users deploy services within an easy-to-use console. Object and Archive storage offer ease of use via APIs. Oracle, in short, has worked to make its implementation user friendly.

## Data Transfer:

To transfer data to the cloud, users can use the public internet to connect to Oracle Cloud Infrastructure. Those who need higher bandwidth for large quantities of data can use Oracle Fast Connect for dedicated 1Gbps or 10Gbps links to connect directly or through exchange partners.

Oracle offers a free storage gateway to allow users to use Object storage without complicated conversions of their applications to use object APIs. Finally, a data transfer appliance also allows customers to ship data to Oracle on pre-built systems that eliminate guesswork and make it easy and cheap to send petabyte-scale data to the cloud.

Advertisement

## Performance:

Oracle Cloud Infrastructure Compute bare metal instances is shown in testing to have a 2X-5X performance advantage with comparable or lower pricing, compared to similar configurations from Amazon Web Services (AWS) across a range of workloads.

## Availability/SLA:

Oracle has an Service Level Agreement that covers availability, manageability and performance, which differentiates from typical SLAs, which cover availability only.

Oracle’s availability, for instance, gives different discounts if service levels are breached in the following areas:

* Block Volumes
* Object Storage
* FastConnect (an enhanced connectivity option)

## Technical Support:

Oracle offers enterprise-class technical support with all its services at no extra charge. A single point of contact provides customers with rapid response support across Cloud, as well as all Oracle software. Oracle has sales, customer support, technical support, portal and documentation in English.

“Tech support was very responsive. Developer outreach people were excellent. Documentation is decent but a little sparse,” said a software engineer in manufacturing.

## Security:

All data is encrypted at rest using frequently rotated keys managed by Oracle. Additional options for customer managed keys and encryption in flight are either available or coming soon.

Advertisement

## Storage Management:

Block storage offers fast copy and clone features that allow instantaneous copies of data to be created, named and restored. Object and archive storage use APIs and lifecycle policies to allow for flexible usage and lifecycle tiering.

## Markets and Use Cases:

Oracle’s OCI Classic offering is suited for users of Oracle databases and applications, while OCI is suited for cloud-native applications and batch computing requirements that benefit from bare-metal servers. Users of existing Oracle products make up the largest percentage of OCI’s customer base. Its cloud platform is also beneficial for organizations that require high performance and low predictable pricing for workloads of all types.

## Pricing:

• Pricing for capacity: Block Storage capacity = $0.0425/GB/Mo inclusive of all performance; File Storage capacity = $0.0425/GB/Mo inclusive of all performance; Object Storage Capacity = $0.0255/GB/Mo; Archival Storage Capacity = $0.0026/GB/Mo

• Pricing for data transfer and/or number of requests: Data transfer appliance & storage gateway services are free. For Internet data egress (inbound free), the first 10TB is free, $0.0085 per GB outbound per month. Object storage requests are charged $0.0034 per 10,000 requests per month.
